historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED pending selector, encoding, collision behavior, audit/session effects and rollback.

original_test_intent: Rename one dedicated BMC test account and verify exact identity, login/audit mapping, collision handling and restoration without altering credentials or privilege.
original_method: Do not guess selector or encoding; require dedicated user, approved non-sensitive name, uniqueness rules, baseline, confirmation, readback and rollback.
manual_activity: Vendor/security owner defines selector/name rules and approves one dedicated account; operator validates uniqueness, access and independent recovery.

command_applicability.command_recommendation: None until exact vendor rename semantics and rollback are approved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Baseline one dedicated account, validate an unused non-sensitive name, rename once, verify readback/login/audit mapping, restore original and compare sessions/roles.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds absent identity-change contract without editing Master.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only name lookup cannot replace rename coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong selector/collision can affect admin login and corrupt audit attribution.

project_override_considerations: Any API must target the same user and provide equivalent encoding, readback, login/audit and rollback evidence.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title requires a security identity mutation but Procedure/Criteria are TBD, and log clearing would destroy attribution evidence.

blocked_analysis.analysis: User selector, name encoding/collision and identity effects define the core operation and cannot be guessed.

review_improvement: Prevents wrong-account rename and makes login/audit attribution plus restoration explicit functional coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC username is both login identity and audit attribution. Without selector, encoding and collision rules, a rename may affect a protected account or produce ambiguous identity; security engineering must resolve these semantics before execution.
